s0101.literal: If trouble arises east or west, long-range plans can tie them down;
s0101.idiomatic: If trouble flares east or west, distant strategy can hold them in check;

s0102.literal: if the enemy is stronger than we, move away to avoid their edge—is that not also good!"
s0102.idiomatic: and if they outmatch us, shift ground and avoid their edge—would that not serve as well!"

s0104.literal: Thereupon he led the army to campaign against Lü Long, routed him utterly, and captured his Right Vice Director Yang Huan.
s0104.idiomatic: He then marched against Lü Long, broke him, and took his right vice director Yang Huan.

s0105.literal: Rutan said to him, "You sleep at ease in a perilous state and never thought to choose a new perch; in old age you are a captive—is that wisdom?"
s0105.idiomatic: Rutan told him, "You rested easy in a doomed realm and never chose a safer master; now, old and a prisoner, can you call that wisdom?"

s0106.literal: Huan said, "I received great favor from the Lü clan and held the second rank; though floods rise to heaven I would still try to save them together—I would be ashamed to appear before a wise lord as a rebel minister."
s0106.idiomatic: Huan said, "The Lü treated me generously and I held the second rank; even if floods covered heaven I would still try to drown with them—I could not face a worthy ruler as a turncoat."

s0107.literal: Rutan said, "You are a loyal minister!"
s0107.idiomatic: Rutan said, "You are a loyal man!"

s0109.literal: Lilugu said to his followers, "I have no talent for ordering the state yet shamefully inherit the enterprise; since I took the throne three years have passed."
s0109.idiomatic: Lilugu told his ministers, "I lack the talent to govern yet hold the throne; three years have passed since I succeeded."

s0110.literal: Though day and night I am reverent, thinking to spread the Way and transform, punishments and government are not yet fair, and customs still decay greatly;"
s0110.idiomatic: "Though I labor day and night to spread the Way, justice is not yet even and customs still decay;"

s0111.literal: war chariots are driven again and again, yet there is no achievement in opening borders;"
s0111.idiomatic: "armies march again and again, yet we win no new ground;"

s0112.literal: I strive to advance worthy men, yet below there is still stagnation.
s0112.idiomatic: "I seek worthy men, yet talent still languishes below."

s0113.literal: Is it that those I employ lack ability, or that my own lack of clarity causes this?"
s0113.idiomatic: "Have I chosen the wrong men, or is my own blindness to blame?"

s0114.literal: You gentlemen, speak without reserve—I shall read your words."
s0114.idiomatic: "Speak plainly, all of you—I will hear it."

s0115.literal: Palace Officer Shi Hao replied, "Ancient kings, when they marched, prized preserving the whole army highest, taking a state second, rescuing the drowning and saving the burning; east or west the people complained."
s0115.idiomatic: Palace officer Shi Hao answered, "Ancient kings, when they took the field, prized sparing the army above all, conquering states second, rescuing the drowning and quenching fire; whether they marched east or west, the people had grievances."

s0116.literal: Now you do not put peace first but make moving households your task; the people love their soil and dread removal, hence there is defection—thus though you behead generals and take cities, the land does not grow."
s0116.idiomatic: "Today you do not put peace first but uproot the people; they love their homes and resist removal, so they rebel—thus you may take cities yet your domain does not widen."

s0117.literal: In choosing scholars and raising talent you first demand bow and horse; letters and arts count as useless—this is not how to draw distant men or leave a lasting name."
s0117.idiomatic: "You choose men by bow and horse alone and treat learning as useless—that will not draw the distant or win lasting fame."

s0118.literal: Confucius said, 'Without learning ritual, one cannot stand.'
s0118.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'Without ritual, a man cannot stand.'

s0119.literal: 'You should build schools, open academies, and choose venerable great scholars to instruct the crown prince's sons.'
s0119.idiomatic: 'Build schools, open halls of learning, and set venerable scholars to teach the sons of the realm.'

s0120.literal: Lilugu approved this and thereupon made Tian Xuanchong and Zhao Yan libationers and masters to teach the crown princes.
s0120.idiomatic: Lilugu agreed and appointed Tian Xuanchong and Zhao Yan libationers to instruct the royal youths.

s0121.literal: At that time, though Lilugu had usurped the title, he still served Yao Xing as a subject.
s0121.idiomatic: Though Lilugu had taken a royal title, he still acknowledged Yao Xing as suzerain.

s0122.literal: Yang Huan's elder brother Jing had aided Yao Chang and died early; Xing heard that Huan had virtue and summoned him.
s0122.idiomatic: Yang Huan's elder brother Jing had served Yao Chang and died young; when Xing heard of Huan's reputation he summoned him.

s0123.literal: Lilugu saw Huan off east of the city and said to him, "I had hoped to achieve the great enterprise with you; affairs have gone against the original plan—the pain of parting is truly as deep as the ancients felt."
s0123.idiomatic: Lilugu feasted Huan east of the city and said, "I meant to build the great enterprise with you; fate has turned—this parting cuts as deep as any in the histories."

s0124.literal: But the kun is not the dark sea and cannot move its body;
s0124.idiomatic: "The great fish is not the ocean deep and cannot swim there;

s0125.literal: the phoenix is not the tall paulownia and cannot dry its wings.
s0125.idiomatic: the phoenix is not the sacred tree and cannot spread its wings."

s0126.literal: You have the talent to aid the age and the treasure of night-shining jade; you should shake your tassels at the Cloud Pavilion and shine in price like linked cities—the mere Hexi right bank is not enough to display your power.
s0126.idiomatic: "You have talent for the times and jewels that shine in the dark; you belong in the halls of empire, worth cities in ransom—Hexi alone cannot hold you."

s0127.literal: Strive daily toward renewal to complete the great beauty."
s0127.idiomatic: "Press on daily and fulfill your promise."

s0128.literal: Huan wept and said, "I formerly served the Lü clan and achieved no merit."
s0128.idiomatic: Huan wept and said, "I served the Lü and achieved nothing for them."

s0129.literal: Your Majesty spared me among the captives and honored me like an old worthy; I always hoped to climb the dragon and cling to the wind and establish merit however small. The dragon gate is now open yet I must leave—the longing of Gongheng—how could I forget it!"
s0129.idiomatic: "Your Majesty raised me from captivity and treated me as an old friend; I hoped to rise with you and do some small service. The gate is open yet I must go—the tie to a true lord—how could I forget it!"

s0131.literal: He sent Rutan again to attack Lü Long's Changsong prefect Meng Yi at Xianmei and took it.
s0131.idiomatic: He sent Rutan to attack Lü Long's Changsong prefect Meng Yi at Xianmei and took the place.

s0132.literal: Rutan seized Yi and rebuked him, saying, "To act when you see the moment is what reward honors first;"
s0132.idiomatic: Rutan seized Yi and said, "To seize the moment wins reward;"

s0133.literal: to hold to error and not change is what punishment reaches.

s0134.literal: I am about to display might at the Jade Gate and sweep Qin and Long; you stubbornly hold a desperate city and delay the royal command—does the state's constant punishment suit your station?"
s0134.idiomatic: "I will show my might at the Jade Gate and sweep Qin and Long; you held a doomed town against the royal command—do you accept the law's due?"

s0135.literal: Yi said, "The enlightened lord has cut down Hexi and his fame fills the realm; with civil virtue he soothes the distant and with martial might he punishes the unyielding—how could Yi, so slight, dare resist Heaven's mandate!"
s0135.idiomatic: Yi said, "Your lordship has conquered Hexi and your name fills the realm; civil virtue wins the distant and martial might punishes the proud—how could I, a nobody, resist Heaven?"

s0136.literal: The punishment of the war drum is Yi's portion.
s0136.idiomatic: "The drum of war is my due."

s0137.literal: But he who is loyal there is also loyal here.
s0137.idiomatic: "Loyalty to one master is loyalty to another."

s0138.literal: I received great favor from the Lü clan and bore the duty of a frontier shield; when the enlightened lord came I submitted, fearing guilt before your staff—only your lordship may judge."
s0138.idiomatic: "The Lü favored me with a frontier post; when you came I submitted, fearing I might seem a traitor—only you can judge."

s0139.literal: Rutan was greatly pleased, released his bonds, and treated him with guest courtesy.
s0139.idiomatic: Rutan was delighted, freed him, and honored him as a guest.

s0140.literal: He moved more than two thousand households from Xianmei and Ligan and returned.
s0140.idiomatic: He resettled more than two thousand households from Xianmei and Ligan and withdrew.

s0141.literal: Honoring Yi's loyal integrity, he appointed him Left Marshal.
s0141.idiomatic: Praising Yi's loyalty, he made him Left Marshal.

s0142.literal: Yi requested, saying, "The Lü clan is about to perish; the holy court's possession of Hexi is already clear."
s0142.idiomatic: Yi said, "The Lü are finished; your taking of Hexi is already plain."

s0143.literal: Yet to guard for others and not succeed, then to bear a lofty post again—I have never been at ease with it.
s0143.idiomatic: "I held a post I could not keep; to take honor again shames me."

s0144.literal: By the enlightened lord's grace, grant that Yi may meet execution at Guzang—death would be undying."
s0144.idiomatic: "By your grace let me die at Guzang—that death would be immortal."

s0145.literal: Rutan, moved by righteousness, granted it.

s0146.literal: Lü Long was attacked by Juqu Mengxun and sent envoys begging for troops; Lilugu gathered his ministers to deliberate.
s0146.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun attacked Lü Long, who begged for aid; Lilugu called his ministers to counsel.

s0147.literal: Left Director of the Masters of Writing Poyan Lun said, "Now Guzang is famine-stricken and ruined; grain is ten thousand cash a picul and there is no green grass in the wilds—supplies cannot be taken."
s0147.idiomatic: Director Poyan Lun said, "Guzang is starving; grain costs ten thousand cash a picul and the fields are bare—there is nothing to feed an army."

s0148.literal: Mengxun marches a thousand li; grain transport cannot follow—let the two foes wear each other down and strike at their lapse."
s0148.idiomatic: "Mengxun marches a thousand li without supplies—let the two enemies weaken each other and strike when they falter."

s0149.literal: If Mengxun takes Guzang he also cannot hold it—it will simply be taken for us; we should not rescue."
s0149.idiomatic: "If Mengxun takes Guzang he cannot hold it—we should take it ourselves, not rescue Long."

s0150.literal: Rutan said, "Lun knows one thing but not the second."
s0150.idiomatic: Rutan said, "Lun sees one side only."

s0151.literal: Though Guzang is now weak and ruined, its ground holds strategic advantage—it is the western meeting place of capitals and cannot be left to Mengxun; we should rescue quickly."
s0151.idiomatic: "Guzang is weak but its ground is strong—the western hub of realms. Mengxun must not hold it; we must rescue at once."

s0152.literal: Lilugu said, "The chariot-and-cavalry commander's words are my own heart."
s0152.idiomatic: Lilugu said, "The chariot commander's words are my own mind."

s0153.literal: Thereupon he sent Rutan with ten thousand horse to rescue him.
s0153.idiomatic: He sent Rutan with ten thousand horse to relieve Long.

s0154.literal: When he reached Changsong, Mengxun had already withdrawn; Rutan moved more than five hundred households from Liangze and Duandui and returned.
s0154.idiomatic: At Changsong Mengxun had already withdrawn; Rutan resettled five hundred households from Liangze and Duandui and returned.

s0155.literal: Lilugu fell ill and ordered, "Within and without there are many troubles and state affairs are weighty—let the chariot-and-cavalry commander succeed to the enterprise to fulfill the former king's will."
s0155.idiomatic: Lilugu fell ill and commanded, "Trouble presses within and without; let the chariot commander succeed and fulfill our father's will."

s0156.literal: He had reigned three years and died; he was buried southeast of Xiping; his posthumous title was King Kang.
s0156.idiomatic: He had ruled three years and died; he was buried southeast of Xiping with the posthumous name King Kang.

s0157.idiomatic: His younger brother Rutan succeeded him.

s0159.literal: Rutan in youth was quick-witted and had talent and stratagem.
s0159.idiomatic: Rutan was quick and resourceful from youth.

s0160.literal: His father marveled at him and told his sons, "Rutan's clear insight and practical skill are not your class."
s0160.idiomatic: His father said to his sons, "Rutan's vision and ability are not yours."

s0161.literal: Therefore the elder brothers did not pass the realm to their sons but wished to transmit it to Rutan.
s0161.idiomatic: So the elder brothers meant the realm for Rutan, not their own sons.

s0162.literal: When Lilugu took the throne he merely held court; all great affairs of army and state were entrusted to him.
s0162.idiomatic: When Lilugu reigned he held court in name only; Rutan ran army and state.

s0163.literal: In the first year of Yuanxing he presumptuously styled himself King of Liang, moved to Ledu, and changed the era name to Hongchang.
s0163.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanxing he took the title King of Liang, moved the capital to Ledu, and proclaimed the era Hongchang.

s0164.literal: Earlier, when Qifu Gangui was at Jinxing, he had left his heir Chibpan as hostage.
s0164.idiomatic: When Qifu Gangui had been at Jinxing, he left his heir Chibpan as hostage.

s0165.literal: Later Chibpan fled back and was seized by pursuing horsemen; Lilugu ordered him killed.
s0165.idiomatic: Chibpan later fled home and was caught by pursuers; Lilugu ordered his death.

s0166.literal: Rutan said, "For a minister or son to flee back to lord and father is a universal principle of old; thus Cao Wu favored Guan Yu's flight and Qin Zhao forgave King Xiang of Chu's departure."
s0166.idiomatic: Rutan said, "A son who flees to his father follows the oldest law; Cao Cao honored Guan Yu's return and King Zhao of Qin spared King Xiang of Chu."

s0167.literal: Though Chibpan fled in rebellion, his filial heart is praiseworthy; he should receive full pardon to extend the measure of sea and mountain."
s0167.idiomatic: "Chibpan fled from loyalty to kinship—that deserves mercy, not death."

s0169.literal: By this time Chibpan had fled again to Yunjie; Rutan returned his wife and children.
s0169.idiomatic: When Chibpan fled again to Yunjie, Rutan sent back his family.

s0170.literal: Yao Xing sent envoys to appoint Rutan General of Chariots and Cavalry and Duke of Guangwu.
s0170.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent envoys naming Rutan General of Chariots and Cavalry and Duke of Guangwu.

s0171.idiomatic: Rutan greatly expanded the walls of Ledu.

s0172.literal: Yao Xing sent General Qi Nan with troops to welcome Lü Long at Guzang; Rutan took over the garrisons of Changsong and Wei'an to avoid him.
s0172.idiomatic: Xing sent General Qi Nan to install Lü Long at Guzang; Rutan seized the garrisons of Changsong and Wei'an to give way.

s0173.literal: Xing's Liangzhou inspector Wang Shang sent Registrar Zong Chang on a friendly mission.
s0173.idiomatic: Wang Shang, Xing's inspector of Liangzhou, sent his registrar Zong Chang as envoy.

s0174.literal: Chang's father Xie, in Lü Guang's time, had entered the capital from Governor of Huanghe as Master of Writing; he met Rutan at Guangwu, took his hand, and said, "Lord, your spirit is lofty and sweeping, your free air towers over clouds—you are a hero of the age and will surely clear the world's troubles."
s0174.idiomatic: Chang's father Xie had been governor of Huanghe under Lü Guang and later master of writing; meeting Rutan at Guangwu he took his hand and said, "You have the air of a hero of the age—you will clear the world's troubles."

s0175.literal: I regret my old age and cannot live to see it; I entrust Chang and his brothers to you."
s0175.idiomatic: "I am too old to see it; I leave my sons to you."

s0176.literal: Now Rutan said to Chang, "With my ordinary talent I was wrongly praised by your late father; I always feared I would stain the great man's mirror-like clarity."
s0176.idiomatic: Rutan told Chang, "Your father praised my small talent; I feared I would shame his judgment."

s0177.literal: When I shamefully inherited the family enterprise, I secretly cherished the gentleman's regard.
s0177.idiomatic: "When I took the realm I still held his kindness in my heart."

s0178.literal: The Odes say, 'Hidden in the center—what day shall I forget it.'
s0178.idiomatic: The Odes say, 'Kept in the heart—when shall I forget?'

s0179.literal: "I never thought that today I would see you."
s0179.idiomatic: "I never thought to see you today."

s0180.literal: Chang said, "Great king, your benevolence matches Wei Zu; in remembering my forebear, though Zhu Hui looked on Zhang Kan's orphan and Shu Xiang raised Qi Zi's son, they could add nothing."
s0180.idiomatic: Chang said, "Your kindness matches Cao Cao's; in honoring my father you surpass even the famous kindnesses of old."

s0181.literal: When the wine was deep they spoke of their whole lives.
s0181.idiomatic: Over wine they spoke of their lives.

s0182.literal: Rutan said, "You are Lu Su's equal—I regret not sharing the great enterprise with you."
s0182.idiomatic: Rutan said, "You are Lu Su's peer—I regret we did not build the realm together."

s0183.literal: Because Yao Xing was strong and Rutan secretly plotted Guzang, he abolished his era name, dismissed Masters of Writing and attendants, and sent Staff Officer Guan Shang as envoy to Xing.
s0183.idiomatic: Seeing Yao Xing's power and plotting Guzang, Rutan dropped his era title, cut court offices, and sent Guan Shang to Xing.

s0184.literal: Xing said to Shang, "The chariot commander offers sincerity and tribute as the state's frontier shield, yet on his own he raises troops and builds a great city—is this how a minister should act?"
s0184.idiomatic: Xing asked Shang, "Your lord submits as a frontier shield, yet raises troops and builds a great city—is that how a vassal behaves?"

s0185.literal: Shang said, "Lords and marquises set defenses to secure themselves—this is the former kings' institution, to settle the people and guard the host and prepare against the unforeseen."
s0185.idiomatic: Shang said, "Princes fortify themselves by ancient rule—to guard their people and meet sudden danger."

s0186.literal: The chariot commander is remote on the frontier, close to fierce foes; south the rebellious Qiang are not yet submitted, west Mengxun is overbearing—it is a double gate for the state; we did not think Your Majesty would suddenly take offense."
s0186.idiomatic: "Your servant sits on the frontier beside strong enemies—Qiang unrest in the south, Mengxun proud in the west. The walls are the realm's outer gate; we did not think you would take offense."

s0187.literal: Xing laughed and said, "Your words are right."

s0188.literal: Rutan sent his general Wenzhi to campaign against the southern Qiang and western barbarians and broke them utterly.
s0188.idiomatic: Rutan sent Wenzhi against the southern Qiang and western tribes and routed them.

s0189.literal: He memorialized Yao Xing requesting Liangzhou; it was not granted, but Rutan was made Regular Attendant with an added fief of two thousand households.
s0189.idiomatic: He asked Xing for Liangzhou and was refused, but was made Regular Attendant with two thousand added households.

s0190.literal: Rutan thereupon led troops against Juqu Mengxun and encamped at Dichi.
s0190.idiomatic: Rutan then marched on Juqu Mengxun and camped at Dichi.

s0191.literal: Mengxun held the city fast; they cut his grain and millet and returned as far as Chiquan.
s0191.idiomatic: Mengxun held his walls; they ravaged his crops and withdrew to Chiquan.

s0192.literal: He presented Xing with three thousand horses and thirty thousand sheep.
s0192.idiomatic: He sent Xing three thousand horses and thirty thousand sheep.

s0193.literal: Xing then appointed Rutan Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs in Hexi, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Colonel Protector of the Xiongnu, Governor of Liangzhou, Regular Attendant and Duke as before, stationed at Guzang.
s0193.idiomatic: Xing then named Rutan commander of Hexi, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, protector of the Xiongnu, governor of Liangzhou, and duke as before, with his seat at Guzang.

s0194.literal: Rutan led thirty thousand foot and horse to encamp at Wujian; Wang Shang, Xing's inspector of Liangzhou, sent Xin Chao, Meng Yi, and Peng Min out to welcome him.
s0194.idiomatic: Rutan led thirty thousand men to Wujian; Wang Shang sent Xin Chao, Meng Yi, and Peng Min to welcome him.

s0195.literal: Shang went out from the Clear Yang Gate; the south-pacifying commander Wenzhi entered from the Cool Wind Gate.
s0195.idiomatic: Shang went out by the Clear Yang Gate; Wenzhi entered by the Cool Wind Gate.

s0196.literal: Zong Chang as vice director escorted Shang back to Chang'an; Rutan said, "I have gained more than three thousand households of Liangzhou whom my heart trusts—you alone, how can you leave me?"
s0196.idiomatic: Zong Chang escorted Shang to Chang'an; Rutan said, "I have won three thousand Liang households I lean on—you above all—how can you leave?"

s0197.literal: Chang said, "Now I escort the old lord—that is loyalty to your highness."
s0197.idiomatic: Chang said, "I serve the old master—that is loyalty to you."

s0198.literal: Rutan said, "I am newly governing this noble province—what policy wins the distant and settles the near?"
s0198.idiomatic: Rutan asked, "I am new to this province—how shall I win the distant and settle the near?"

s0199.literal: Chang said, "Though Liang soil is worn, it is ground of strategic advantage; the Way is advanced by men—it lies with your highness."
s0199.idiomatic: Chang said, "Liang is weary but strong in position; men make the Way—it rests with you."

s0200.literal: Duan Yi and Meng Yi are longstanding hopes of Wuwei;
s0200.idiomatic: Duan Yi and Meng Yi are the old pillars of Wuwei;
